text: The fatal night, a few moments later: the clang Helen hears, which Holmes reads as Dr. Roylott hastily closing his safe upon the snake
why: ¶50 places the clang a few moments after the whistle on the fatal night, and ¶249 gives Holmes's explanation that Roylott was closing the safe.

text: Half an hour later: the creature hisses, a very gentle sound like a small jet of steam from a kettle
why: ¶236 describes the kettle-like sound after half an hour, and ¶249 identifies it as the creature's hiss.

text: That instant: Holmes attacks the creature with his cane at the bell-pull
why: ¶236 says that the instant they heard it Holmes lashed with his cane at the bell-pull, and ¶249 confirms he attacked the creature.

text: Next day, travelling back: Holmes tells of the chair, the safe, the milk and the whipcord, and of the clang
why: ¶247 sets Holmes's account on the journey back next day, and ¶249 covers the chair, safe, milk, whipcord and clang.

text: Before Holmes inspects it: Dr. Roylott has been in the habit of standing on his chair to reach the ventilator
why: ¶249 states that the chair inspection showed he had been in the habit of standing on it to reach the ventilator.

text: In Dr. Roylott's chamber: the safe, the saucer of milk and the loop of whipcord dispel Holmes's last doubts
why: ¶249 states that the sight of the safe, milk and whipcord dispelled any remaining doubts, and ¶¶158-169 place them in Roylott's chamber.

text: Why did Julia strike a light? — she heard the snake hiss in the room
id: q.why_match=she heard the snake hiss in the room
why: A reasonable possibility: Julia struck a light when alarmed (¶55), and Holmes struck his on hearing the hiss (¶236, ¶249).

text: Why did the whistle sound just as Holmes struck the light?
why: ¶238 states that the whistle was heard at the moment Holmes struck the light, so the question arises naturally and does not point to an answer.

text: Why did the whistle sound just as Holmes struck the light? — he saw the light through the ventilator and called the snake home
id: q.whistle_at_match=he saw the light through the ventilator and called the snake home
why: A reasonable possibility: ¶229 says Roylott would see a light through the ventilator, and ¶248 says the whistle recalled the snake.

text: Why did the whistle sound just as Holmes struck the light? — it was already time for the recall, and the match only happened to coincide
id: q.whistle_at_match=it was already time for the recall, and the match only happened to coincide
why: A plain alternative possibility, since ¶248 establishes the whistle as a recall signal and nothing yet settles why it sounded at that moment.
